chapter: Chicago radio, Whiteman and courting Mildred
title: Jitterbug dancers lead him to Louis and Earl Hines
summary: Two black jitterbug dancers he worked with at the Oriental take him to a South Side club to hear Louis Armstrong with Earl Hines.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Couple times we used to go around here
cause I could tell you one little story, when I was working with Paul Ash, -- there was a dance team, a black dance team. They were jitterbuggers --
And they'd won all the contests at the Ballrooms Aragon and the Trianon, all-around and they were --
-- kids and they got married, too. But I worked a couple of dates out of town with them--
-- and we got talking and I had those records by Louis and Earl Hines. You know, 'Waiting for a Date'
And those records that they had made and I had those and I was playing them. And, so we did a date out of town, I don't remember what it was -- down in Illinois somewhere -- [End of Reel II, Side 1]
Okay, Red now you were telling me a story there and -- we ran out of tape.
The two jitterbug dancers, they'd won all the contests in the theaters and they were doing -- I met them at the Oriental Theater, the prize was so many weeks work, at the Publix Theaters --

And they conducted in all the pub -- Public Theaters -- Balaban and Katz Theaters in Chicago. So they used to hear me play on these records, and I was playing Monday Date and things by Louie Armstrong -- and they said that they had worked at a club on the South Side, and that they'd worked in the show. And that how Louie used to come out on the floor and just play to them and really sell them.
-- so they took me over to the place, it was upstairs, that's when I first them, that little band of Earl's and-I mean of Louie's -- with Earl's.
No, it was a place called the Back-- maybe -- Black and Tan, or I guess it was the Sunset -- it was upstairs -- I know, I always mean to ask Earl the name of that place --
I asked him once and I forgot the name of it.
I think it could've been the Sunset or it was the Black and Tan -- not sure.
There was a change of name, too. So Stan will know, we'll ask him after.
It was kind of wild, I enjoyed, it yeah.
Yeah, those kids were wonderful dancers --
But that's when I got to hearing -- I went back a number of times to hear him. And then later Earl had the band at the Grand Terrace, I used to go down there, of course.
Yeah. Well when you went down -- that was before you'd met Mildred?
No, not at the Terrace but the --
This was when I was just started a single with Paul Ash (unintelligible).
